1	# Task 10: Walking spider from primitives
2	
3	Build a single-page browser app with the provided framework, served by vite, rendering to the canvas with id #app. Show a spider made only from simple geometric shapes (a body made of two or more primitives and eight jointed legs, each leg having at least two segments) walking in place on a flat ground plane. The legs must move in an alternating gait: legs on opposite diagonals move together, and each leg visibly lifts, swings forward and plants again. The body should bob slightly with each step. The motion must loop seamlessly with a period of about 2 seconds and run continuously without user input. Use a neutral studio-style backdrop with soft lighting and shadows so the shape reads clearly from a three-quarter camera that frames the whole spider. Do not load external model files.
4	
5	## Rendering contract (all tasks)
6	
7	- Draw into the existing `<canvas id="app">` (640x360 CSS pixels, device pixel ratio 1). Do not resize it or create another canvas.
8	- Render continuously with `requestAnimationFrame`. When the first frame has been drawn set `window.__EVAL_READY__ = true`.
9	- No network access: load assets only from `/assets/...` (served from `public/assets`). Do not import from CDNs.
10	- Code goes in `src/` (TypeScript, strict). The entry is `src/main.ts`. It must pass `typecheck` and build with `vite build`.
11	- When you are done, call `finish`.
12

2

content.thinking:
I'm designing a spider rig with a body made of abdomen and cephalothorax spheres, plus eight legs built from hip, upper segment, knee, and lower segment pieces, animated with quaternion tracks for a seamless two-second walking loop.

For the gait, I'm setting up diagonal leg groups that alternate swing and stance phases across the cycle, with a body bob synced to two steps per loop, and positioning each hip joint around the body's perimeter with an outward-facing base yaw so the legs radiate naturally from the torso.

Working out the nested hip rotation hierarchy now so swing and lift angles compose correctly for each side...

I'll set up hip and shoulder as nested quaternion-rotated nodes plus a knee bend joint, aiming for a resting pose where the upper leg segment angles up and out while the lower segment angles down to reach the ground, then work out the geometry so the foot height matches the ground plane correctly.

For the walk cycle, I'll make the swing phase lift the foot by increasing shoulder pitch and knee bend, while during stance I'll keep the foot approximately planted even though the simplified IK will introduce some slight sliding.

Yaw changes don't affect foot height, so stance foot height stays constant with fixed pitch, though body bob of ~0.025-0.03 will make feet slightly sink or float, which I'll just accept rather than compensate for. For stride length, with horizontal reach of about 1.39 from hip, swinging the yaw amplitude ±0.28 rad gives a stride arc of roughly 0.78.

Since this is walking in place, the feet effectively slide like a treadmill under a stationary body, which I'll treat as acceptable. I'm defining the swing and stance phases: swing covers the first half of the cycle with yaw sweeping from -A to +A using a smoothstep and a sine-based lift curve, while stance covers the second half with a linear yaw return, with leg group B offset by half a cycle. I'm setting up keyframes at a 0.05s sampling rate and composing the hip rotation quaternion.

Working out the shoulder and knee joint angles to produce the right foot-lift height, I'm finding the combined lift from upper and lower segments comes out larger than intended, so I need to reduce the lift coefficient.

I'm assigning each leg a forward-backward angle offset so front legs point forward and back legs point backward, with hip z-positions spaced along the body.

For the leg segments, I'm building tapered cylinder geometry rotated so its axis runs along X, with joint spheres at the knee and hip and a small foot cone at the tip.

For the body, I'm shaping the cephalothorax and abdomen as scaled spheres positioned relative to each other, adding small black eye spheres, and skipping pedipalps and fangs for simplicity. The legs are nested under the body group so the idle bob animation moves everything together, and I'm working out the exact foot height by summing the vertical offsets from each leg segment's angle relative to the hip position.

I'm checking the leg reach versus body width to make sure the spider's overall span fits the camera framing, then syncing the body's subtle bobbing motion with the gait cycle so it dips slightly when legs transition between ground contact groups, possibly adding a touch of roll or pitch for realism.

For the scene setup, I'll let the bridge handle native camera and lighting, writing a three-quarter camera angle in the recipe and checking what lights and shadow settings it emits by default. I'll add a flat ground plane with a neutral backdrop, check the "product-studio" look preset, then import and inspect the resulting scene file before refining further.
